newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran seeks world help for 60,000 Kurd refugees.
newsitem.headline: Iran seeks world help for 60,000 Kurd refugees.

text.p: Iran appealed on Sunday for international aid for thousands of Iraqi Kurd refugees it said it was sheltering after they fled recent fighting in Iraq.

In an Iranian television report quoted by the British Broadcasting Corporation, Ahmad Hosseini, Iran's top official in charge of refugees, said that Iran was sheltering 60,000 refugees in six border camps in its western provinces.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran has so far spent 20 billion rials on assisting the Iraqi Kurdish refugees. The United Nations and other international organisations, despite their declarations that they were willing to help, have so far not supplied any kind of assistance to the Islamic Republic," he was quoted as saying.
"He called on the governments of the world and the United Nations not to turn away from this enormous human tragedy," the TV said.
The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Saturday in Geneva an inspection team had so far found about 30,000 Kurdish refugees in camps on the Iranian side of the border.
The UNHCR has assigned $3.6 million from its emergency fund to provide shelter, food and medicines for the refugees.
The medical relief group Medecins Sans Frontieres also said it launched an emergency operation to help tens of thousands of Kurdish refugees who have fled into Iran.
The refugees fled the takeover of northern Iraq by the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) faction.
The Iranian news agency said on Sunday refugees were rushing to the border "in a state of panic" over reports that the Iraqi army and KDP forces "were preparing to attack" refugees.
